BusinessRuleException

class BusinessRuleException(message, *, code=None, details=None)[source]

Bases: Exception

Exception raised when a business rule is violated.

This exception is designed to handle specific business logic violations with optional error codes and additional details for error tracking and debugging.

Parameters:
messagestr

The exception message describing the business rule violation.

codestr | None, optional

Error code that identifies the type of violation (keyword-only). Default is None.

detailsdict[str, Any] | None, optional

Additional details about the exception (keyword-only). Default is None, stored as an empty dictionary.

Attributes:
messagestr

The exception message describing the business rule violation.

codestr | None

An optional error code to identify the type of violation.

detailsdict[str, Any]

A dictionary containing additional details about the exception.

Methods

__str__()

Return a string representation of the exception, formatted with code prefix if available.

__repr__()

Return a detailed string representation containing all exception attributes.

Notes

message is also passed to Exception.__init__, so it is available in args[0].

A falsy details (None or an empty mapping) is replaced by a new empty dictionary. A falsy code (None or "") is omitted from str().

Examples

>>> exc = BusinessRuleException("Invalid age", code="E01")
>>> str(exc)
'[E01] Invalid age'
>>> str(BusinessRuleException("Invalid age"))
'Invalid age'
>>> exc.details
{}
